title: Courtesy Transportation Agreements Held Over Time
content:
Training note for the central support desk on how many Courtesy Transportation Agreements a customer may have over time.

## The rule

A customer may have Courtesy Transportation Agreements over time without limit. No program of the Courtesy Transportation Agreements sets a maximum number of agreements per customer across time; the number a customer may have out at the same moment is a separate matter, governed by the open-agreement limit.

## The same rule, put another way

| Question the rule answers | Answer under this rule |
|---|---|
| Is there a lifetime or yearly ceiling on the number of loaner agreements one customer may sign? | No. Agreements over time are without limit. |
| Does this rule decide how many agreements may be out at once? | No. How many may be out at once is governed by the open-agreement limit, not by this rule. |
| Does the program a past agreement was written under change this answer? | No. The absence of a limit over time holds for every program. |

## Hypothetical illustration

A customer who, over several years, has driven a dozen loaners on a dozen separate repair visits, every agreement long since returned, has reached no ceiling under this rule: the history of agreements, however long, sets no limit. The number of visits is invented for the example.
